senses.definition: accepted or habitual practice
the act of using
examples: he warned against the use of narcotic drugs
skilled in the utilization of computers

senses.definition: the customary manner in which a language (or a form of a language) is spoken or written
examples: English usage
a usage borrowed from French

senses.definition: (economics) the utilization of economic goods to satisfy needs or in manufacturing
examples: the consumption of energy has increased steadily

senses.definition: (law) the exercise of the legal right to enjoy the benefits of owning property
examples: we were given the use of his boat

senses.definition: (psychology) an automatic pattern of behavior in reaction to a specific situation; may be inherited or acquired through frequent repetition
examples: owls have nocturnal habits
she had a habit twirling the ends of her hair
long use had hardened him to it

senses.definition: a particular service
examples: he put his knowledge to good use
patrons have their uses

senses.definition: exerting shrewd or devious influence especially for one's own advantage
examples: his manipulation of his friends was scandalous

senses.definition: the act of using
examples: he warned against the use of narcotic drugs
skilled in the utilization of computers

senses.definition: what something is used for
examples: the function of an auger is to bore holes
ballet is beautiful but what use is it?

senses.definition: avail oneself to
examples: apply a principle
practice a religion
use care when going down the stairs
use your common sense
practice non-violent resistance

senses.definition: habitually do something or be in a certain state or place (use only in the past tense)
examples: She used to call her mother every week but now she calls only occasionally
I used to get sick when I ate in that dining hall
They used to vacation in the Bahamas
she used to be his best friend and now they are enemies

senses.definition: put into service; make work or employ for a particular purpose or for its inherent or natural purpose
examples: use your head!
we only use Spanish at home
I can't use this tool
Apply a magnetic field here
This thinking was applied to many projects
How do you utilize this tool?
I apply this rule to get good results
use the plastic bags to store the food
He doesn't know how to use a computer

senses.definition: seek or achieve an end by using to one's advantage
examples: She uses her influential friends to get jobs
The president's wife used her good connections

senses.definition: take or consume (regularly or habitually)
examples: She uses drugs rarely

senses.definition: use up (resources or materials)
examples: this car consumes a lot of gas
We exhausted our savings
They run through 20 bottles of wine a week

senses.definition: (of persons) taken advantage of
examples: after going out of his way to help his friend get the job he felt not appreciated but used

senses.definition: employed in accomplishing something
examples: the principle of surprise is the most used and misused of all the principles of war

senses.definition: previously used or owned by another
examples: bought a secondhand (or used) car

senses.definition: in the habit of doing something
examples: … was wont to complain that this is a cold world

senses.definition: in the habit of or adapted to
examples: accustomed to doing her own work
I've grown accustomed to her face
we are used to better service in this restaurant

senses.definition: being of use or service
examples: the girl felt motherly and useful
a useful job
a useful member of society

senses.definition: having a useful function
examples: utilitarian steel tables

senses.definition: having no beneficial use or incapable of functioning usefully
examples: a kitchen full of useless gadgets
she is useless in an emergency

senses.definition: a person who makes use of a thing; someone who uses or employs something
a person who takes drugs
a person who uses something or someone selfishly or unethically
an official stationed at the entrance of a courtroom or legislative chamber
someone employed to conduct others
take (someone) to their seats, as in theaters or auditoriums
examples: he ushered us to our seats

senses.definition: commonly encountered
examples: a common (or familiar) complaint
the usual greeting

senses.definition: occurring or encountered or experienced or observed frequently or in accordance with regular practice or procedure
examples: grew the usual vegetables
the usual summer heat
came at the usual time
the child's usual bedtime

senses.definition: under normal conditions
examples: usually she was late
